guard: the connector arms its event plane from the launch flag alone, never from a grant it happens to hold, and refuses an armed launch that gives the write-ahead log nowhere to live
why: Arming and authorization are two facts about one session, and the whole risk is that they get
treated as one. An agent file or a manifest can hand-write anything into allowPublish, so a
connector that read the grant as an instruction would let any author who can write an agent file
turn on a full transcript of another seat's tool inputs and outputs, without ever touching the
launch grammar or passing a manager refusal.
The write-ahead log's home is the same shape of failure one layer down. A log under the launch
working directory is invisible to the next start, so the next start reads an already-published
thread as virgin and republishes sequence numbers the stream has seen. That is not a degraded
mode, it is a corrupted one, so the launch refuses rather than defaults.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY. The suite imports the connector by relative source path (../src/extension.js)
and calls buildLaunch directly: no dist in the path, no build in the command, no child process.
Its one package-name import is core's eventChannel, which two cells deliberately compare the
connector against and no mutation below replaces.

mutations.name: A1 read the grant as an instruction, the confusion the suite is named for
mutations.expectRed: a hand-written event-channel grant does NOT arm the emitter
mutations.cell: a hand-written event-channel grant does NOT arm the emitter
mutations.note: Written the way it would plausibly be written: it looks like the connector helpfully noticing what it is allowed to do.

mutations.name: A2 default the write-ahead log to the working directory instead of refusing
mutations.expectRed: an armed launch with no workspace root refuses
mutations.cell: an armed launch with no workspace root refuses
mutations.note: The fallback that looks harmless at the first start and republishes the thread at the second.

mutations.name: A3 re-derive the channel locally with a display-name sanitizer
mutations.expectRed: the connector's channel IS core's derivation, character for character
mutations.cell: the connector's channel IS core's derivation, character for character
mutations.note: A second derivation agrees with core's for most inputs and disagrees for exactly the ones a sanitizer touches, so the failure surfaces as an auth rejection at publish time rather than at launch.
